protocol.py: 6 biology problems (2 errors, 1 warning, 3 notes).

1. ERROR WELL-CAPACITY: More liquid than the well can hold: 500 ul in a 368 ul well, 1 well
   line 42:  p1000.dispense(500, well)
   At line 42 the robot filled well A1 in slot 4 past the rim (368 ul to the rim by the
   labware definition's shape; the maker states 200 ul), reaching 500 ul. The liquid runs
   into the neighbouring wells and onto the deck; the volumes still add up on paper, so the
   plate map does not see it, and the simulator says nothing. Wells: well A1 in slot 4.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Fix: Use labware with bigger wells, or scale every volume down so the fullest well stays
   under the stated maximum with room to mix.
   Source: Opentrons labware schema 2: totalLiquidVolume, the total well volume in
   microlitres
           https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opentrons/opentrons/edge/shared-data/labware/schemas/2.json
   Source: Bartley et al. 2023, LabOP: a protocol never adds more liquid than its container
   holds
           https://jakebeal.github.io/Publications/JETC23-LabOP.pdf
   [27d8fda67a63]

2. ERROR WELL-CAPACITY: More liquid than the well can hold: 500 ul in a 368 ul well, 6 wells
   line 49:  p1000.dispense(250, well)
   At line 49 the robot filled wells B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 4 past the rim (368
   ul to the rim by the labware definition's shape; the maker states 200 ul) (this line did
   it 6 times), reaching 500 ul. The liquid runs into the neighbouring wells and onto the
   deck; the volumes still add up on paper, so the plate map does not see it, and the
   simulator says nothing. Wells: wells B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 4.
   Affected: wells B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 4.
   Fix: Use labware with bigger wells, or scale every volume down so the fullest well stays
   under the stated maximum with room to mix.
   Source: Opentrons labware schema 2: totalLiquidVolume, the total well volume in
   microlitres
           https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opentrons/opentrons/edge/shared-data/labware/schemas/2.json
   Source: Bartley et al. 2023, LabOP: a protocol never adds more liquid than its container
   holds
           https://jakebeal.github.io/Publications/JETC23-LabOP.pdf
   [38febaff95c7]

3. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: Mixing too weak to stir 6 wells: 3 × 150 ul in 500 ul
   line 51:  p1000.mix(3, 150, well)
   At line 51 the tip mixes wells B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 4 with 3 strokes of 150
   ul in a well holding 500 ul (this line did it 6 times). 3 strokes of 150 ul move 0.9 of
   the well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of strokes to mix (the mixing work).
   Integra draws over 80% of the well five times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty
   gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated, and in a
   dilution series every later step inherits the error.
   Affected: wells B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 4.
   Fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (400 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 400,
   well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [16d479dbc398]

4. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No blank on a dilution series: 7 wells of standard
   line 42:  p1000.dispense(500, well)
   At line 42 the robot starts a dilution series of standard in NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL
   Flat (slot 4): 7 wells at 7 concentrations, each level about 2 times weaker than the one
   before. No well on this plate holds diluent with no sample, so there is no blank: the
   curve has no zero to read against, and a signal from the diluent or the plastic cannot be
   told from the lowest point. Wells: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and G1 in slot 4.
   Fix: Add a well of diluent alone, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [3decb91be949]

5. NOTE WELL-CAPACITY: Declared more than the well holds: 2000 ul in a 1898 ul well, 1 well
   line 45:  p1000.aspirate(250, diluent_well)
   At line 45 the robot draws from tube A2 in slot 2, which the protocol declares (line 28)
   to hold 2000 ul; the well holds 1897.79 ul. The prep sheet cannot be followed as written.
   Wells: tube A2 in slot 2.
   Affected: tube A2 in slot 2.
   Fix: Declare what the well can really hold, or use a bigger container.
   Source: Opentrons labware schema 2: totalLiquidVolume, the total well volume in
   microlitres
           https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opentrons/opentrons/edge/shared-data/labware/schemas/2.json
   Source: Bartley et al. 2023, LabOP: a protocol never adds more liquid than its container
   holds
           https://jakebeal.github.io/Publications/JETC23-LabOP.pdf
   [6202a11fa7b7]

6. NOTE CONTAM-WELL: A used tip carried diluent (tube A2 in slot 2) into well A1 in slot 4
it was never meant for
   line 48:  p1000.aspirate(250, prev_well)
   At line 48 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 4 while it still carried diluent
   (tube A2 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a
   little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into
   this well on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different
   samples, each now holds a little of another. Liquid was later taken out of the affected
   wells, and the unwanted material went along into 2 other wells: wells A1 and A2 in slot
   6.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Also reached 2 other wells: wells A1 and A2 in slot 6.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 48. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense
   from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is
   already in the well.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   [3bab0717957e]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
